title: HTTP/3 WebSocket Local Peer Proof Harness Architecture
purpose: Define a repeatable local-loopback peer proof for the existing RFC 9220 WebSocket-over-HTTP/3 tunnel surface.
design_summary: The local peer proof keeps the production `Http3Client` and `Http3Server` APIs in the test path and drives a single accepted WebSocket Extended CONNECT tunnel through request/response metadata, server ping and client pong helper behavior, text exchange, a buffered 6000-byte binary exchange, client close, and server close echo. The PowerShell proof wrapper runs only that aggregate test, stores TRX/stdout/stderr under `.artifacts/http3-websocket-local-peer/<run-id>`, and emits JSON/Markdown manifests with SHA256 hashes.
data_and_state_considerations: The proof is intentionally local-loopback peer evidence: client and server run in the same test process but communicate over the public QUIC and HTTP/3 APIs rather than direct parser helpers. The aggregate test complements the existing requirement-home tests without changing WebSocket support scope or claiming external interoperability.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The proof requires platform QUIC listener and connection support; unsupported local platforms return from the xUnit test consistently with the existing loopback tests.
The 6000-byte binary payload crosses the default WebSocket tunnel read-buffer size to exercise buffered frame assembly.
The generated artifacts are local evidence, not external peer, isolated-host, ProtocolLab publishable, or remote CI evidence.
risks: The harness can only prove the in-repo client/server pair until an external WebSocket-over-H3 peer is wired.
The proof does not cover production proxy target, authorization, timeout, or deployment policy.
